title: Image Processing

definition: Image Processing is a core concept in MERN Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Image Processing is
theory.body: Image Processing describes the methods and patterns used within MERN Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Image Processing is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Image Processing matters
theory.body: Without Image Processing, systems built with MERN Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Image Processing works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Image Processing follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Image Processing.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Image Processing
theory.body: Image Processing offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
